records.source: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἐπορεύετο, καὶ προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπιδεῖξαι αὐτῷ τὰς οἰκοδομὰς τοῦ ἱεροῦ·
records.gloss: And having gone out the Jesus from the temple was going, and came the disciples of him to point out to him the buildings of the temple;
pieces: As Jesus came out of the temple and went on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples approached to point out its buildings to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.1: And Jesus went out from the temple and was going away, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came to point out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the buildings of the temple.

R.1: Jesus left the temple courts and was walking away. His followers came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They wanted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to look at the temple buildings.

decisions.choice: the temple: the whole temple area with its courts and buildings, rebuilt on a grand scale by Herod the Great
decisions.reason: Herod began rebuilding the temple about 20 BC, and the work went on for decades. The word covers the whole complex, whose great stones and halls the disciples admired.

decisions.choice: Jesus leaves the temple: the scene follows his words that the house is left desolate (23:38)
decisions.reason: Matthew places Jesus's departure straight after his lament over Jerusalem. What the disciples admire is what he has just said will be left desolate.

decisions.choice: temple courts; followers
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Jesus left the whole temple area, and calls the disciples his followers, as in 12:1.

records.heading: Not one stone on another

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ βλέπετε ταῦτα πάντα;
records.gloss: He but answering said to them, Not do you see these things all?
pieces: In answer {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "You see all this, do you not?

L.2: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to them, "Do you not see all these things?

R.2: Jesus answered them, "Do you see all these buildings?

decisions.choice: do you not see all these things: a question that expects "yes" and turns their admiration toward what will happen to the buildings
decisions.reason: The disciples have pointed out the buildings. Jesus asks them to look again, because of what he is about to say.

decisions.choice: these buildings
decisions.reason: Readable says what "these things" are: the buildings the disciples pointed out.

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ ἀφεθῇ ὧδε λίθος ἐπὶ λίθον ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you, not not will be left here stone upon stone which not will be thrown down.
pieces: Truly I tell you, every stone here will be pulled down, until not one is left resting on another."

L.2: Truly I tell you, there will certainly not be left here a stone upon a stone that will not be thrown down."

R.2: I tell you the truth, all of this will be torn down. Not one stone will be left on top of another."

decisions.choice: will certainly not be left: a double negative, a firm prediction
decisions.reason: The Greek uses its strongest form of denial. Jesus says the destruction will be complete.

decisions.choice: the prediction of the temple's destruction
decisions.reason: Roman forces destroyed the temple in AD 70, when they took Jerusalem. Prophets had spoken in the same way of the first temple (Micah 3:12; Jeremiah 26:18).

decisions.choice: will be thrown down: a passive, the destroyer is not named
decisions.reason: The verb means to pull down or demolish. Jesus does not say who will do it.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

decisions.choice: the pulling down first, then the picture of the stones
alternatives: no stone will be left on another that will not be thrown down
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the double negative into a plain statement and keep the picture of the stones.

records.source: Καθημένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοῦ Ὄρους τῶν Ἐλαιῶν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ κατ’ ἰδίαν λέγοντες· Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν πότε ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον τῆς σῆς παρουσίας καὶ συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος.
records.gloss: Sitting and him on the Mount of the Olives came to him the disciples privately saying, Tell us when these things will be, and what the sign of your coming and of end of the age.
pieces: Later, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by themselves and said, "Tell us when this will take place. And what sign will mark {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} coming and the close of the age?"

L.3: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} privately, saying, "Tell us, when will these things be, and what [will be] the sign of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} coming and of [the] end of the age?"

R.3: Later Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives. The disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was alone. They said, "Tell us, when will these things happen? What will be the sign that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are coming and that the end of this age is here?"

decisions.choice: coming: arrival, the word used of a ruler's visit; here the coming of Jesus in glory
decisions.reason: The word can mean presence or arrival. Matthew uses it only in this chapter (24:3, 27, 37, 39), each time of the coming of the Son of Man.

decisions.choice: two questions: when the temple will fall, and what sign will mark his coming and the end of the age
decisions.reason: One article joins "your coming" and "the end of the age", so the disciples treat them as one event. They seem to link it with the fall of the temple.

decisions.choice: the end of the age: the close of the present age, when God judges and sets all things right
alternatives: the end of the physical world
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the phrase for the harvest at the end (13:39-40, 49) and for the limit of Jesus's promise to be with his disciples (28:20).

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: perhaps recalling the Lord standing there on the day of judgment
decisions.reason: The Mount of Olives faces the temple across the Kidron Valley. Zechariah 14:4 says the Lord's feet will stand on it on that day. Matthew does not draw the link himself.

decisions.choice: by themselves (B); when he was alone (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "privately" means: away from the crowds.

records.heading: The first birth pains

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς πλανήσῃ·
records.gloss: And answering the Jesus said to them, See lest anyone you mislead;
pieces: Jesus replied, "Be on your guard, so that nobody leads you astray.

L.4: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Take care that no one misleads you.

R.4: Jesus answered, "Be careful! Do not let anyone fool you.

decisions.choice: said: the start of the last of Jesus's five long speeches in Matthew, which runs through 25:46
decisions.reason: The speech answers the disciples' question and goes on to the end of chapter 25. Like the others it ends "when Jesus had finished" (26:1; compare 7:28; 11:1; 13:53; 19:1).

decisions.choice: take care, mislead: be on guard against being led astray
decisions.reason: The verb "see" is used as a warning. "Mislead" means to make someone wander from the right way, and it returns in 24:5, 11 and 24. The first danger Jesus names is deception.

decisions.choice: take care (L); be on your guard (B); be careful (R)
decisions.reason: Each level uses a common English warning for the verb "see".

records.source: πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ χριστός, καὶ πολλοὺς πλανήσουσιν.
records.gloss: Many for will come in the name of me saying, I am the Christ, and many they will mislead.
pieces: Many will come and use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, saying, 'I am the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},' and they will lead many astray.

L.5: For many will come in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, saying, 'I am the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},' and they will mislead many.

R.5: Many people will come and use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. They will say, 'I am the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}!' And they will fool many people.

decisions.choice: in my name: claiming the title and authority that belong to Jesus
decisions.reason: To come in someone's name is to claim to act for them, or to be them. These people take for themselves what belongs to Jesus.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, the anointed king God promised
decisions.reason: With the article the word is a title. These deceivers claim to be the promised king. Matthew spells out the claim that Mark 13:6 gives only as "I am".

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: The Greek has the article, so every level writes "the" before the title, with Christ or Messiah as the reader chooses.

records.source: μελλήσετε δὲ ἀκούειν πολέμους καὶ ἀκοὰς πολέμων· ὁρᾶτε, μὴ θροεῖσθε· δεῖ γὰρ γενέσθαι, ἀλλ’ οὔπω ἐστὶν τὸ τέλος.
records.gloss: You will be about and to hear of wars and reports of wars; see, not be alarmed; it must for happen, but not yet is the end.
pieces: You are going to hear of wars, and of news of wars. Take care not to be shaken. These things have to happen, but that does not mean the end has come.

L.6: And you are going to hear of wars and reports of wars. See [that] you are not alarmed; for it must happen, but the end is not yet.

R.6: You will hear the noise of wars nearby and news of wars far away. Do not let it frighten you. These things must happen. But it is not yet the end.

decisions.choice: reports of wars: news of wars elsewhere
decisions.reason: Wars nearby are heard; wars far off are heard about. The phrase covers both.

decisions.choice: it must happen: part of what God has planned
decisions.reason: "Must" expresses God's purpose, as in Daniel 2:28, where God shows what must happen in the last days.

decisions.choice: the end: the end of the age the disciples asked about (24:3)
decisions.reason: Wars are not the signal that the end has come. The word returns in 24:13 and 24:14.

decisions.choice: news of wars (B); the noise of wars nearby and news of wars far away (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the second phrase means instead of keeping the old pairing.

records.source: ἐγερθήσεται γὰρ ἔθνος ἐπὶ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν, καὶ ἔσονται λιμοὶ καὶ σεισμοὶ κατὰ τόπους·
records.gloss: Will rise for nation against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in places;
pieces: Nation will go to war with nation, and kingdom with kingdom. In one place after another there will be famines and earthquakes.

L.7: For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in [various] places.

R.7: Countries will fight against each other. Kingdoms will attack other kingdoms. In many places people will go hungry, and there will be earthquakes.

decisions.choice: nation against nation, kingdom against kingdom: in the words of Isaiah 19:2
decisions.reason: Isaiah 19:2 speaks of city against city and kingdom against kingdom in God's judgment on Egypt (compare 2 Chronicles 15:6). Jesus uses the prophets' language for the troubles ahead.

decisions.choice: in places: here and there, in one place after another
decisions.reason: The phrase means throughout different places.

decisions.choice: famines and earthquakes, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: famines and plagues and earthquakes, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and plagues", which is in Luke 21:11. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: people will go hungry
decisions.reason: Readable says what a famine is.

records.source: πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων.
records.gloss: All but these beginning of birth pains.
pieces: Yet all of this is only the start of the birth pains.

L.8: But all these [are the] beginning of birth pains.

R.8: But all these things are only the beginning of the pain. It is like the first pains of a woman about to give birth.

decisions.choice: the beginning of birth pains: the first of the sufferings that come before God's new age
decisions.reason: The prophets used a woman's labor as a picture of the distress before God acts (Isaiah 26:17-19; Micah 4:9-10). Labor pains are hard but lead to new life, and these are only the first of them.

decisions.choice: It is like the first pains of a woman about to give birth.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture.

records.source: Τότε παραδώσουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς θλῖψιν καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.
records.gloss: Then they will hand over you to affliction and will kill you, and you will be being hated by all the nations because of the name of me.
pieces: Then they will hand you over for harsh treatment and kill you, and all the nations will hate you because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

L.9: Then they will hand you over to tribulation and will kill you, and you will be hated by all the nations because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

R.9: Then people will arrest you and make you suffer. They will kill you. People of every nation will hate you because you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: tribulation: pressure, suffering, persecution
decisions.reason: The word means pressure and so great trouble. It returns for the great distress of 24:21 and 24:29.

decisions.choice: because of my name: because you belong to me
alternatives: because you speak my name aloud
decisions.reason: As in 10:22, a name stands for the person. They will be hated for being his.

decisions.choice: by all the nations: by people everywhere, Jews and Gentiles
decisions.reason: In 10:22 they are hated "by all". Here the hatred reaches all the nations, to whom the gospel will be proclaimed (24:14).

decisions.choice: people will arrest you and make you suffer
alternatives: they will hand you over to tribulation
decisions.reason: Readable says who "they" are and what being handed over means.

decisions.choice: because you belong to me
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom, as in 10:22.

records.source: καὶ τότε σκανδαλισθήσονται πολλοὶ καὶ ἀλλήλους παραδώσουσιν καὶ μισήσουσιν ἀλλήλους·
records.gloss: And then will be caused to stumble many and one another will hand over and will hate one another;
pieces: Many will then fall away, handing each other over and hating each other.

L.10: And then many will be caused to stumble, and they will hand one another over and will hate one another.

R.10: Then many people will stop following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They will turn against each other and hate each other. They will hand each other over to the authorities.

decisions.choice: be caused to stumble: fall away from faith in Jesus
decisions.reason: The verb means to trip. In Matthew it is used of those who give up following Jesus under pressure (13:21; 26:31).

decisions.choice: one another: within the circle of those who followed Jesus
decisions.reason: As in 10:21, the betrayal comes from the inside. Those who fall away turn against those who stay.

decisions.choice: stop following me; to the authorities
alternatives: be caused to stumble; hand over
decisions.reason: Readable says what stumbling and handing over mean here.

records.source: καὶ πολλοὶ ψευδοπροφῆται ἐγερθήσονται καὶ πλανήσουσιν πολλούς·
records.gloss: and many false prophets will arise and will mislead many;
pieces: False prophets will rise up in great numbers, and they will lead many astray.

L.11: And many false prophets will arise and will mislead many.

R.11: Many people will come who say they speak for God but do not. They will fool many others.

decisions.choice: false prophets: those who claim to speak for God but lead people astray
decisions.reason: As in 7:15, they come from within. Israel had long been warned against them (Deuteronomy 13:1-5; Jeremiah 23:16).

decisions.choice: people who say they speak for God but do not
decisions.reason: Readable says what a false prophet is, as in 7:15.

records.source: καὶ διὰ τὸ πληθυνθῆναι τὴν ἀνομίαν ψυγήσεται ἡ ἀγάπη τῶν πολλῶν.
records.gloss: and because of the being multiplied the lawlessness will grow cold the love of the many.
pieces: As lawlessness spreads, most people's love will cool.

L.12: And because lawlessness will be multiplied, the love of the many will grow cold.

R.12: People will break God's law more and more. Because of this, the love most people have will grow cold.

decisions.choice: lawlessness: disregard for God's law, wickedness
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the word for the evil of those who do not do God's will (7:23; 13:41; 23:28).

decisions.choice: the love of the many: the love that most people have for God and for one another
decisions.reason: The verse follows the betrayal and hatred of 24:10, so love for one another is in view. The text does not say whose love, and love for God may be included.

decisions.choice: break God's law
decisions.reason: Readable says whose law is meant.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.
records.gloss: The but having endured to end, this one will be saved.
pieces: But whoever holds out to the end will be saved.

L.13: But the one who endures to [the] end, this [one] will be saved.

R.13: But anyone who stays faithful to the end will be saved.

decisions.choice: the same saying as 10:22
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats what he told the Twelve when he sent them out. The wording is kept the same as in 10:22 at each level.

decisions.choice: to the end: to the end of the trial, even if it brings death
alternatives: to the end of the age only
decisions.reason: There is no article, and the phrase can mean "to the very end". It may also look to "the end" of 24:6 and 24:14. Either way one must hold firm however long the trouble lasts.

decisions.choice: will be saved: rescued for life in God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Some will be killed (24:9), so this is rescue beyond death, as in 10:22.

decisions.choice: holds out (B); stays faithful (R)
decisions.reason: As in 10:22, Balanced and Readable use everyday words for enduring.

records.source: καὶ κηρυχθήσεται τοῦτο τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ οἰκουμένῃ εἰς μαρτύριον πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, καὶ τότε ἥξει τὸ τέλος.
records.gloss: And will be proclaimed this the gospel of the kingdom in whole the inhabited world for a testimony to all the nations, and then will come the end.
pieces: This gospel of the kingdom will be announced throughout the world, so that every nation hears the witness, and only then will the end come.

L.14: And this gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed in the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.

R.14: This good news about God's kingdom will be told everywhere in the world. People of every nation will hear it. Then the end will come.

decisions.choice: this gospel of the kingdom: the good news Jesus himself proclaims, that God's rule has come near
alternatives: a later message about Jesus only
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the phrase for Jesus's preaching (4:23; 9:35). "This" points to the message of Jesus's own teaching.

decisions.choice: the inhabited world: all the lands where people live
decisions.reason: The word means the inhabited earth. Here it stands beside "all the nations" and means everywhere people live (compare 28:19).

decisions.choice: as a testimony to all the nations: so that they hear the witness
decisions.reason: As in 10:18, the phrase can mean a witness to people or against them. Here the gospel is proclaimed so that the nations hear it before the end comes.

decisions.choice: the world
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the world"; the meaning decision explains that the word means the inhabited world.

decisions.choice: good news about God's kingdom
decisions.reason: As in 4:23, Readable says "good news" and whose kingdom it is.

records.source: Ὅταν οὖν ἴδητε τὸ βδέλυγμα τῆς ἐρημώσεως τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Δανιὴλ τοῦ προφήτου ἑστὸς ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ, ὁ ἀναγινώσκων νοείτω, τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη, ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος μὴ καταβάτω ἆραι τὰ ἐκ τῆς οἰκίας αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω ὀπίσω ἆραι τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: When therefore you see the abomination of the desolation, the spoken through Daniel the prophet, standing in place holy (the reading let him understand), \v 16 then those in the Judea let them flee to the mountains, \v 17 the on the housetop not let him come down to take the things out of the house of him, \v 18 and the in the field not let him turn back behind to take the cloak of him.
pieces: So when you see the abomination that brings ruin, of which the prophet Daniel spoke, standing in the holy place (let the reader take note),
then those in Judea must escape to the hills.
Anyone on the roof must not go down to fetch things from the house,
and anyone in the field must not turn back for a cloak.

L.15: So when you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in [the] holy place (let the one reading understand),
L.16: then let those in Judea flee to the mountains;
L.17: let the one on the housetop not come down to take the things out of {{gender:their|his}} house,
L.18: and let the one in the field not turn back to take {{gender:their|his}} cloak.

R.15: The prophet Daniel spoke about 'the horrible thing that brings ruin.' One day you will see it standing in the holy place. (Reader, think carefully about what this means.)
R.16: When that happens, people in Judea must run away to the hills.
R.17: If someone is up on the roof of a house, they must not go down to get anything from inside.
R.18: If someone is working in the field, they must not go back to get their coat.

decisions.choice: the abomination of desolation: the phrase from Daniel 9:27, 11:31 and 12:11
decisions.reason: In Daniel it is a detestable thing set up in God's sanctuary that leaves it desolate. In 167 BC the Syrian king Antiochus IV set up a pagan altar on the temple altar, and 1 Maccabees 1:54 uses the same phrase for it. Jesus says something like it will happen again.

decisions.choice: standing in the holy place: in the temple
decisions.reason: Daniel speaks of the sanctuary, and the holy place most naturally means the temple. Here, unlike Mark 13:14, the word "standing" agrees with the thing, not with a person.

decisions.choice: let the one reading understand: an aside to the reader of the Gospel
alternatives: Jesus urging his hearers to understand Daniel when they read it
decisions.reason: The words speak of reading, not hearing, so they are most likely the Gospel writer's aside, as in Mark 13:14. They may instead be Jesus's call to understand what Daniel wrote, since Daniel too is told to understand (Daniel 9:23, 25).

decisions.choice: the housetop, the cloak: flat roofs reached by an outside stair, and the outer garment laid aside for work
decisions.reason: One could leave a flat roof by the outside stair without going indoors. A worker in the field laid the cloak aside. The danger will be so sudden that there is no time even for these.

decisions.choice: their or his (L); anyone ... a cloak (B); someone ... they (R)
decisions.reason: The commands apply to anyone. Literal offers "their" or "his" through the gender setting; Balanced and Readable use "anyone" and "they".

decisions.choice: the abomination that brings ruin (B); the horrible thing that brings ruin (R); let the reader take note (B); Reader, think carefully about what this means (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Daniel's phrase as it is. Balanced and Readable say what it means. Every level keeps the aside in parentheses.

records.heading: Flee to the mountains

records.source: οὐαὶ δὲ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
records.gloss: Woe but to those in womb having and to those nursing in those the days.
pieces: Woe to women who are pregnant and to those nursing babies in those days!

L.19: And woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!

R.19: Those days will be very hard for women who are pregnant, and for mothers who are nursing babies.

decisions.choice: having in the womb: pregnant
decisions.reason: "To have in the womb" is the ordinary Greek way of saying a woman is pregnant.

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and pity
decisions.reason: Here "woe" is not a curse on these women. It grieves for them, because they will find it hardest to flee.

decisions.choice: woe (L, B); will be very hard (R)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Matthew, Literal and Balanced keep "woe". Readable says what the cry means.

records.source: προσεύχεσθε δὲ ἵνα μὴ γένηται ἡ φυγὴ ὑμῶν χειμῶνος μηδὲ σαββάτῳ·
records.gloss: Pray but that not may happen the flight of you in winter nor on Sabbath;
pieces: Pray that you will not have to escape in winter, or on a Sabbath day.

L.20: And pray that your flight may not happen in winter, nor on a Sabbath.

R.20: Pray that you will not have to run away in the winter or on the Sabbath, the day of rest.

decisions.choice: winter: the cold, rainy season
decisions.reason: In Judea winter is the rainy season. Streams run high and roads turn to mud, so flight on foot would be hard.

decisions.choice: on a Sabbath: when travel was limited and help hard to find
alternatives: a rule that disciples must not flee on the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Jewish custom limited how far one walked on the Sabbath (compare Exodus 16:29; Acts 1:12), and town gates and shops would be shut. Only Matthew mentions the Sabbath here, which may show that his first readers kept it.

decisions.choice: the day of rest
decisions.reason: Readable says what the Sabbath is, as in 12:1.

records.source: ἔσται γὰρ τότε θλῖψις μεγάλη οἵα οὐ γέγονεν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς κόσμου ἕως τοῦ νῦν οὐδ’ οὐ μὴ γένηται.
records.gloss: Will be for then affliction great such as not has happened from beginning of world until the now nor not not may happen.
pieces: For that will be a time of great distress, worse than anything that has happened since the world began, and nothing like it will ever happen again.

L.21: For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not happened from [the] beginning of [the] world until now, nor ever will.

R.21: It will be a time of terrible trouble. Nothing like it has happened since the world began, and nothing like it will ever happen again.

decisions.choice: great tribulation such as has not happened: in the words of Daniel 12:1
decisions.reason: Daniel 12:1 speaks of a time of distress such as has never been since there was a nation. Jesus widens it to the whole history of the world.

decisions.choice: nor ever will: a double negative
decisions.reason: The strongest form of denial: there will never be another time like it.

decisions.choice: tribulation (L); distress (B); terrible trouble (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the long-used word, as in 24:9. Balanced and Readable use everyday words for great suffering.

records.source: καὶ εἰ μὴ ἐκολοβώθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι, οὐκ ἂν ἐσώθη πᾶσα σάρξ· διὰ δὲ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς κολοβωθήσονται αἱ ἡμέραι ἐκεῖναι.
records.gloss: And if not were shortened the days those, not would be saved all flesh; because of but the elect will be shortened the days those.
pieces: Had those days not been cut short, not one person would come through alive. But for the sake of the chosen they will be cut short.

L.22: And if those days had not been cut short, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect those days will be cut short.

R.22: If God did not make that time shorter, no one would live through it. But God will make it shorter for the sake of the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen.

decisions.choice: cut short: a passive, God is the one who shortens the days
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action. Mark 13:20 names him: the Lord shortened the days.

decisions.choice: any flesh: any human being
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for living people. "No flesh" means no one.

decisions.choice: be saved: survive, come through alive
decisions.reason: Here the word speaks of living through the distress, not of salvation at the end as in 24:13.

decisions.choice: the elect: the people God has chosen
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures the chosen are God's people. In this speech they are those who belong to God through Jesus (24:24, 31; compare 22:14).

decisions.choice: come through alive (B); live through it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that survival is meant, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: God did not make that time shorter; the people he has chosen
alternatives: those days had not been cut short; the elect
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who shortens the days and says what "the elect" means.

records.source: τότε ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Ἰδοὺ ὧδε ὁ χριστός, ἤ· Ὧδε, μὴ πιστεύσητε·
records.gloss: Then if anyone to you says, Look here the Christ, or Here, not believe;
pieces: If anyone says to you then, 'Look, the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is here!' or 'He is here!' refuse to believe it.

L.23: Then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here [is] the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}!' or 'Here!' do not believe [it].

R.23: At that time someone may tell you, 'Look, the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is here!' or 'He is over here!' Do not believe them.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the promised king, said to have appeared in some place
decisions.reason: People will claim that the Messiah has come and can be found here or there. Jesus says his coming will not be like that (24:27).

decisions.choice: here, or here: two claims about different places
decisions.reason: The Greek repeats "here". Each speaker points to a different place.

decisions.choice: look
decisions.reason: In speech the word points to something said to be in front of them, so it is kept at every level, as in 12:2.

decisions.choice: He is here (B); He is over here (R)
decisions.reason: The second claim is a single word in the Greek. Balanced and Readable make it a full saying. "He" is the claimed Messiah, not Jesus, so it takes no deity_pronoun span.

records.source: ἐγερθήσονται γὰρ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται, καὶ δώσουσιν σημεῖα μεγάλα καὶ τέρατα ὥστε πλανῆσαι εἰ δυνατὸν καὶ τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς·
records.gloss: Will arise for false christs and false prophets and they will give signs great and wonders so as to mislead, if possible, even the elect;
pieces: People falsely claiming to be the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} will rise up, and false prophets with them. They will work great signs and wonders, enough to lead astray even the chosen ones, if such a thing could be done.

L.24: For false {{christos:christs|messiahs}} and false prophets will arise, and they will give great signs and wonders, so as to mislead, if possible, even the elect.

R.24: People will come who falsely say they are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}. Others will falsely claim to be prophets. They will do great signs and amazing things. They will try to fool even God's chosen people, if they can.

decisions.choice: false christs: people who falsely claim to be the Messiah
decisions.reason: The word joins "false" and "Christ". It means pretenders to the title, as in 24:5.

decisions.choice: false prophets with signs and wonders: as in Deuteronomy 13:1-3
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 13:1-3 warns that a prophet may give a sign or wonder that comes true and still lead people astray. Signs alone do not prove a messenger is from God.

decisions.choice: if possible: they will try, but it may not be possible
decisions.reason: The phrase shows how strong the deception will be. It also suggests that God will keep his chosen ones from being led away (24:22).

decisions.choice: people falsely claiming to be the Messiah (B, R); the chosen ones (B); God's chosen people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the compound word means. Readable also says whose chosen people they are.

records.source: ἰδοὺ προείρηκα ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: Look, I have told beforehand you.
pieces: Mark this: I have warned you in advance.

L.25: Look, I have told you beforehand.

R.25: I am warning you now, before it happens.

decisions.choice: I have told you beforehand: the warning stands
decisions.reason: The perfect tense means the warning has been given and remains in force. When these things happen, the disciples will know they were told.

decisions.choice: look (L); Mark this (B); I am warning you now (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

records.source: ἐὰν οὖν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν· Ἰδοὺ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἐστίν, μὴ ἐξέλθητε· Ἰδοὺ ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις, μὴ πιστεύσητε·
records.gloss: If therefore they say to you, Look in the wilderness he is, not go out; Look in the inner rooms, not believe;
pieces: So if they tell you, 'Look, he is in the wilderness,' stay where you are. If they say, 'Look, he is hidden indoors,' do not believe it.

L.26: So if they say to you, 'Look, he is in the wilderness,' do not go out; 'Look, in the inner rooms,' do not believe [it].

R.26: So if people tell you, 'Look, he is out in the desert,' do not go there. If they say, 'Look, he is hiding in a back room,' do not believe it.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: where would-be deliverers gathered their followers
decisions.reason: Leaders claiming to bring God's rescue led crowds out into the wilderness (compare Acts 21:38). Israel looked for a new deliverance like the exodus.

decisions.choice: the inner rooms: hidden rooms inside a house, a secret place
decisions.reason: The same word is used in 6:6 for the inner room where one prays. Some will say the Messiah is hidden away, known only to a few.

decisions.choice: look
decisions.reason: As in 24:23, the word is part of what people say, so it is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: he, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: "He" is the one people claim is the Messiah, so the pronoun takes no span.

decisions.choice: stay where you are (B); he is hidden indoors (B); he is hiding in a back room (R)
alternatives: do not go out; in the inner rooms
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the second claim a full saying and say plainly what not going out means.

records.source: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ ἀστραπὴ ἐξέρχεται ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ φαίνεται ἕως δυσμῶν, οὕτως ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
records.gloss: Just as for the lightning goes out from east and shines as far as west, so will be the coming of the Son of the Man;
pieces: The coming of the Son of Man will be like lightning that flashes in the east and lights up the sky all the way to the west.

L.27: For just as the lightning comes out from [the] east and shines as far as [the] west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

R.27: When the Son of Man comes, everyone will see it. It will be like lightning that flashes across the whole sky from east to west.

decisions.choice: like lightning: sudden and seen by everyone
decisions.reason: Lightning cannot be hidden in a room or a desert. The coming of the Son of Man will not need anyone to point it out (24:23-26).

decisions.choice: coming: the arrival of the Son of Man in glory, as in 24:3
decisions.reason: The same word as in the disciples' question.

decisions.choice: the coming of the Son of Man first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the subject first so the comparison is clear.

decisions.choice: everyone will see it
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the comparison, following the meaning decision.

records.source: ὅπου ἐὰν ᾖ τὸ πτῶμα, ἐκεῖ συναχθήσονται οἱ ἀετοί.
records.gloss: Wherever if may be the corpse, there will be gathered the eagles.
pieces: Where there is a dead body, that is where vultures flock.

L.28: Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will gather.

R.28: Wherever there is a dead body, vultures will gather there.

decisions.choice: vultures: birds that gather at a dead body
decisions.reason: The word usually means eagle, and the eagle was the standard of the Roman legions, so some see a picture of Roman armies here. But the birds gather at a corpse, which is what vultures do, and the word was used of them too (compare Job 39:27-30).

decisions.choice: a proverb: the coming will be as plain as circling birds that show where a body lies
alternatives: judgment will fall wherever it is deserved
decisions.reason: The saying follows the picture of lightning (24:27), so it most likely means the coming cannot be missed. Luke 17:37 gives it in answer to the question "where?". Some read it of judgment falling on what is dead.

records.source: Εὐθέως δὲ μετὰ τὴν θλῖψιν τῶν ἡμερῶν ἐκείνων ὁ ἥλιος σκοτισθήσεται, καὶ ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς, καὶ οἱ ἀστέρες πεσοῦνται ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.
records.gloss: Immediately but after the affliction of the days those the sun will be darkened, and the moon not will give the light of it, and the stars will fall from the heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
pieces: Right after the distress of those days the sun will turn dark and the moon will stop giving its light. Stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

L.29: And immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

R.29: As soon as that time of terrible trouble is over, the sun will become dark. The moon will not shine. Stars will fall from the sky. The powers in the heavens will be shaken.

decisions.choice: sun, moon and stars: in the words of Isaiah 13:10 and 34:4
alternatives: a new prophecy with no source
decisions.reason: Isaiah 13:10 says the sun will be dark and the moon will not give its light; Isaiah 34:4 says the host of heaven will fall. Joel 2:10 speaks the same way.

decisions.choice: darkened sun and falling stars: the prophets' language for God acting in judgment
alternatives: only a description of the physical sky
decisions.reason: Isaiah used these words of the fall of Babylon (Isaiah 13). Such language marks a great act of God that shakes the world. How literally it is meant here is not certain.

decisions.choice: the powers of the heavens: the heavenly bodies, or spiritual powers ruling there
decisions.reason: "Powers" can mean the sun, moon and stars as the host of heaven, or spiritual beings. Both were thought of together.

decisions.choice: sky
decisions.reason: The same Greek word means both sky and heaven. Where stars fall, Balanced and Readable say sky.

records.heading: The Son of Man on the clouds of heaven

records.source: καὶ τότε φανήσεται τὸ σημεῖον τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ τότε κόψονται πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς·
records.gloss: And then will appear the sign of the Son of the Man in heaven, and then will mourn all the tribes of the earth and they will see the Son of the Man coming on the clouds of the heaven with power and glory great;
pieces: Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Every tribe on earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on heaven's clouds, with power and great glory.

L.30: And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.

R.30: Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. All the peoples of the earth will cry out in sorrow. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds in the sky with power and great glory.

decisions.choice: the sign of the Son of Man: the sign the disciples asked for (24:3), perhaps the Son of Man himself appearing
alternatives: a separate sign in the sky, such as a banner or a cross
decisions.reason: The disciples asked for the sign of his coming. The verse does not say what it is. It may be the Son of Man himself, seen in heaven, or a signal that goes before him (compare the banner of Isaiah 11:12).

decisions.choice: all the tribes will mourn: in the words of Zechariah 12:10-14
decisions.reason: Zechariah says the people will look on the one they pierced and mourn, tribe by tribe. Here the mourning spreads to all the tribes of the earth.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven: Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: In Daniel one like a son of man comes with the clouds of heaven and is given authority, glory and an everlasting kingdom. Jesus will say the same before the high priest (26:64).

decisions.choice: the tribes of the earth: the peoples of the whole earth
alternatives: the tribes of the land of Israel
decisions.reason: The same words can mean "the tribes of the land", as in Zechariah. Beside the coming seen by all (24:27), they most likely mean all peoples.

decisions.choice: the sky (B, R); heaven's clouds (B); the clouds in the sky (R)
alternatives: in heaven; the clouds of heaven
decisions.reason: The same Greek word means sky and heaven. Balanced keeps Daniel's "clouds of heaven"; Readable says sky throughout.

decisions.choice: peoples; cry out in sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable uses common words, following the meaning decision on "tribes".

records.source: καὶ ἀποστελεῖ τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ μετὰ σάλπιγγος μεγάλης, καὶ ἐπισυνάξουσιν τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ἀνέμων ἀπ’ ἄκρων οὐρανῶν ἕως τῶν ἄκρων αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And he will send the angels of him with trumpet great, and they will gather together the elect of him from the four winds from ends of heavens to the ends of them.
pieces: As a great trumpet sounds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels. They will gather {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen ones from the four winds, from the farthest edges of the heavens on every side.

L.31: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather together {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} elect from the four winds, from [one] end of [the] heavens to [the other] end of them.

R.31: A loud trumpet will sound, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels. They will gather the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen from every direction, from one end of the sky to the other.

decisions.choice: the trumpet and the gathering: God's promise to gather his scattered people
decisions.reason: Isaiah 27:13 speaks of a great trumpet that calls the scattered home. Deuteronomy 30:4 promises to gather Israel even from the end of the heavens, and Zechariah 2:6 speaks of the four winds. Now the Son of Man gathers the chosen.

decisions.choice: the four winds, from end to end of the heavens: from every direction, everywhere
decisions.reason: The four winds are north, south, east and west. The ends of the heavens are where the sky seems to meet the earth on every side.

decisions.choice: his angels, his elect: the Son of Man has the angels and the chosen people as his own
alternatives: the angels and elect of God only
decisions.reason: What the Scriptures say belongs to God is here said to belong to the Son of Man, as in 13:41.

decisions.choice: with a great trumpet, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: with a trumpet and a great sound
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add a word for "sound" or "call". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the people he has chosen
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the elect" means, as in 24:22.

records.source: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς συκῆς μάθετε τὴν παραβολήν· ὅταν ἤδη ὁ κλάδος αὐτῆς γένηται ἁπαλὸς καὶ τὰ φύλλα ἐκφύῃ, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος·
records.gloss: From but the fig tree learn the parable: when already the branch of it becomes tender and the leaves it puts out, you know that near the summer;
pieces: Take the fig tree as your lesson. When its branches turn soft and leaves start to sprout, you can tell that summer is not far off.

L.32: Now from the fig tree learn the parable: when its branch has already become tender and puts out its leaves, you know that summer [is] near.

R.32: Learn a lesson from the fig tree. When its branches become green and soft and new leaves start to grow, you know that summer is coming soon.

decisions.choice: the fig tree's leaves: a sign that summer is near
decisions.reason: Many trees in the land of Israel keep their leaves all year. The fig loses its leaves in winter, and new ones come in late spring, so its leaves show that summer is near.

decisions.choice: the parable: a comparison that teaches a lesson
decisions.reason: Here the parable is a short comparison from nature.

decisions.choice: the fig tree: perhaps recalling the fig tree of 21:18-21
decisions.reason: Earlier a fig tree without fruit withered at Jesus's word. Here the fig tree's new leaves show that something is near.

decisions.choice: lesson
decisions.reason: Here the word means the lesson the fig tree teaches.

records.heading: Summer is near

records.source: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε πάντα ταῦτα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἐπὶ θύραις.
records.gloss: So also you, when you see all these things, know that near it is, at doors.
pieces: So it is with you: once you see all these things, be sure that it is close, standing at the door.

L.33: So also you, when you see all these things, know that [it] is near, at [the] doors.

R.33: In the same way, when you see all these things happen, you can be sure that the time is near. It is as close as someone standing at the door.

decisions.choice: it is near: the subject is not stated; the end, or the coming of the Son of Man
alternatives: he is near: the Son of Man himself
decisions.reason: The verb has no subject, so it can mean "it is near" or "he is near". Luke 21:31 says "the kingdom of God is near". The coming of 24:30 is what is near in either reading.

decisions.choice: all these things: the troubles and signs of 24:4-28
alternatives: the darkening of the sun and the coming itself
decisions.reason: "These things" are what come before the end, as in the disciples' question (24:3).

decisions.choice: at the doors: very close
alternatives: at the doors of the temple
decisions.reason: To be at the door is to be about to come in.

decisions.choice: the time is near
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject as the time of these events, which keeps both readings open as far as English allows.

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα ταῦτα γένηται.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you that not not will pass away the generation this until all these things happen.
pieces: Truly I tell you, all these things will happen before this generation has passed away.

L.34: Truly I tell you that this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things take place.

R.34: I tell you the truth: the people living now will not all die before all these things happen.

decisions.choice: this generation: the people living in Jesus's own time
alternatives: the generation that sees the signs
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in Matthew "this generation" means Jesus's contemporaries (11:16; 12:41-45; 23:36). Others take it as the people of Israel or the generation alive when the signs begin. The meaning depends on what "all these things" includes.

decisions.choice: all these things: the events of 24:4-28, including the fall of the temple
alternatives: everything in the speech, including the coming of the Son of Man
decisions.reason: "All these things" in 24:33 are the signs that come before the end. Read that way, Jesus says his own generation will see them, while the day itself no one knows (24:36).

decisions.choice: will certainly not: a double negative, a firm promise
decisions.reason: The strongest form of denial.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The same forms as in 24:2.

decisions.choice: the people living now
decisions.reason: Readable follows the reading chosen above. If that reading is wrong, this wording says more than the Greek.

records.source: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσεται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρέλθωσιν.
records.gloss: The heaven and the earth will pass away, the but words of me not not will pass away.
pieces: Heaven and earth will pass away; {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words never will.

L.35: Heaven and earth will pass away, but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words will certainly not pass away.

R.35: The sky and the earth will come to an end, but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words will last forever.

decisions.choice: heaven and earth pass, my words remain: as God's word stands forever
decisions.reason: Isaiah 40:8 says the word of our God stands forever, and Isaiah 51:6 says the heavens will vanish like smoke. Jesus says of his own words what the prophets said of God's word (compare 5:18).

decisions.choice: will certainly not pass away: a double negative
decisions.reason: The strongest denial: his words will never fail.

decisions.choice: come to an end; last forever
decisions.reason: Readable uses plainer words for passing away and never passing away.

records.source: Περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης καὶ ὥρας οὐδεὶς οἶδεν, οὐδὲ οἱ ἄγγελοι τῶν οὐρανῶν οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός, εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ μόνος.
records.gloss: Concerning but the day that and hour no one knows, not even the angels of the heavens nor the Son, except the Father alone.
pieces: No one knows the day or the hour when that will come. The angels in heaven do not know it, and neither does the Son. Only the Father knows.

L.36: But concerning that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of the heavens, nor the Son, but the Father alone.

R.36: But no one knows on what day or at what hour this will happen. The angels in heaven do not know. Even the Son does not know. Only the Father knows.

decisions.choice: nor the Son, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the words left out, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: "Nor the Son" is in some of the earliest manuscripts, such as Codex Sinaiticus as first written and Codex Vaticanus, and is missing from many later ones, perhaps because copyists found it hard. Nearly all manuscripts have it in Mark 13:32. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: nor the Son: Jesus says that he, the Son, does not know the day
alternatives: the Son knows but will not tell
decisions.reason: The Father alone has set the day. The text does not explain how the Son, who shares the Father's knowledge (11:27), does not know it while he lives among people.

decisions.choice: that day and hour: the time of the Son of Man's coming
alternatives: the day of the temple's fall
decisions.reason: "That day" is the prophets' phrase for the day of the Lord. Here it is the day of the coming described in 24:30-31.

decisions.choice: when that will come (B); this will happen (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the list into short sentences and say what the day is.

records.heading: Keep watch, for the day is unknown

records.source: ὥσπερ γὰρ αἱ ἡμέραι τοῦ Νῶε, οὕτως ἔσται ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
records.gloss: Just as for the days of the Noah, so will be the coming of the Son of the Man;
pieces: The coming of the Son of Man will be like the days of Noah.

L.37: For just as the days of Noah [were], so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

R.37: When the Son of Man comes, it will be like it was in the time of Noah.

decisions.choice: the days of Noah: the time before the flood, Genesis 6-7
decisions.reason: The next verses say what Jesus means: people went on with ordinary life and did not see the judgment coming.

decisions.choice: coming: as in 24:3 and 24:27
decisions.reason: The same word for the arrival of the Son of Man.

records.source: ὡς γὰρ ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταῖς πρὸ τοῦ κατακλυσμοῦ τρώγοντες καὶ πίνοντες, γαμοῦντες καὶ γαμίζοντες, ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας εἰσῆλθεν Νῶε εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν, καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν ἕως ἦλθεν ὁ κατακλυσμὸς καὶ ἦρεν ἅπαντας, οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ἡ παρουσία τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
records.gloss: As for they were in the days the before the flood eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until which day entered Noah into the ark, \v 39 and not they knew until came the flood and took away all, so will be also the coming of the Son of the Man.
pieces: Before the flood, people carried on with their meals and their drinking, with weddings for themselves and their children, right up to the day Noah went into the ark.
They had no idea what was coming until the flood came and swept every one of them away. The coming of the Son of Man will be like that too.

L.38: For as in the days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark,
L.39: and they did not know until the flood came and took them all away, so also will be the coming of the Son of Man.

R.38: Before the great flood, people were eating and drinking. They were getting married and giving their children to be married. They kept on doing this until the day Noah went into the big boat.
R.39: They did not know what was going to happen until the flood came and carried them all away. It will be the same when the Son of Man comes.

decisions.choice: Noah entered the ark, the flood took them away: Genesis 7:7-23
decisions.reason: Noah went into the ark and the flood came and wiped out everyone outside it.

decisions.choice: eating, drinking, marrying, giving in marriage: ordinary daily life
decisions.reason: Men married, and fathers gave their daughters in marriage. Jesus does not name any sin here. The danger is that people went on as usual, unaware.

decisions.choice: they did not know: they were unaware of what was coming
decisions.reason: The point is not that no warning was given but that they paid no attention until it was too late.

decisions.choice: weddings for themselves and their children (B); giving their children to be married (R); what was coming (B, R)
alternatives: marrying and giving in marriage; they did not know
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who gave in marriage and what they did not know.

decisions.choice: big boat
decisions.reason: Readable says what the ark was.

records.source: τότε δύο ἔσονται ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, εἷς παραλαμβάνεται καὶ εἷς ἀφίεται·
records.gloss: Then two will be in the field, one is taken and one is left;
pieces: Two people will then be working in the field: one is taken, and the other is left.

L.40: Then two will be in the field; one is taken and one is left.

R.40: At that time two people will be working in a field. One will be taken, and the other will be left behind.

decisions.choice: taken, left: taken to be with the Son of Man, or left for judgment
alternatives: taken away in judgment, as by the flood, and left to live
decisions.reason: The verb "taken" is used of taking someone along as a companion (1:20; 17:1), and the angels gather the chosen in 24:31. But the flood "took" people away in judgment (24:39), so some read the one taken as judged. The verse stresses the sudden separation more than which is which.

decisions.choice: is taken, is left: present tense of a future event
decisions.reason: The present makes the scene vivid. It will happen then.

decisions.choice: two people ... working
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "two". Balanced and Readable say they are people at work; the next verse speaks of women, so this one is not limited to men.

records.source: δύο ἀλήθουσαι ἐν τῷ μύλῳ, μία παραλαμβάνεται καὶ μία ἀφίεται.
records.gloss: two grinding at the mill, one is taken and one is left.
pieces: Two women will be grinding grain at the mill: one is taken, and the other is left.

L.41: Two [women will be] grinding at the mill; one is taken and one is left.

R.41: Two women will be grinding grain with a millstone. One will be taken, and the other will be left behind.

decisions.choice: grinding at the mill: grinding grain into flour, women's daily work at home
alternatives: a large mill run by animals
decisions.reason: Grain was ground by hand each day with a pair of stones. The Greek forms show that the two are women.

decisions.choice: women (L in brackets; B, R); grain (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek words are feminine, so every level says women. Balanced and Readable say what was ground.

records.source: γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε ποίᾳ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ κύριος ὑμῶν ἔρχεται.
records.gloss: Keep awake therefore, because not you know on what day the Lord of you comes.
pieces: So stay alert, since you do not know which day your Lord will come.

L.42: Keep watch therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.

R.42: So keep watching and be ready! You do not know what day your Lord will come.

decisions.choice: keep watch: stay awake and alert
decisions.reason: The verb means to stay awake. Here it means to be ready for the Lord's coming. It returns in 24:43, 25:13 and at Gethsemane (26:38-41).

decisions.choice: your Lord: Jesus, the Son of Man whose coming is described
decisions.reason: The verses around speak of the coming of the Son of Man (24:39, 44). He is the disciples' Lord.

decisions.choice: on what day, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: at what hour, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "hour", as in 24:44. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: stay alert (B); keep watching and be ready (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what keeping awake means here.

records.source: ἐκεῖνο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ φυλακῇ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται, ἐγρηγόρησεν ἂν καὶ οὐκ ἂν εἴασεν διορυχθῆναι τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: That but know that if had known the master of the house in what watch the thief comes, he would have kept awake and not would have allowed to be dug through the house of him.
pieces: Think about this. A homeowner who knew at what time of night a thief was coming would stay awake and not allow anyone to dig through the walls of his house.

L.43: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have let his house be dug through.

R.43: Think about this. Suppose the owner of a house knew what time of night a robber would come. He would stay awake. He would not let the robber break into his house.

decisions.choice: watch: a part of the night
decisions.reason: The night was divided into watches, four in the Roman reckoning (14:25). A thief comes at night, at a time no one expects.

decisions.choice: be dug through: broken into through the wall
decisions.reason: Many houses had walls of mud brick, which a thief could dig through (6:19).

decisions.choice: the thief: a picture of an arrival no one expects
alternatives: a picture of the Son of Man's character
decisions.reason: Only the timing is compared. The same picture is used of the day of the Lord in 1 Thessalonians 5:2.

decisions.choice: Think about this, then the example told as a fact (B) or a supposition (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the contrary-to-fact sentence into a plain example.

records.source: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὥρᾳ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται.
records.gloss: Because of this also you be ready, because in which not you think hour the Son of the Man comes.
pieces: So you too must stay prepared: the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not imagine.

L.44: Because of this you also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.

R.44: So you must always be ready too. The Son of Man will come at a time when you do not think {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come.

decisions.choice: be ready: a present command, keep on being ready
decisions.reason: Since the hour is unknown, readiness must last.

decisions.choice: is coming: a present tense of something certain to happen
alternatives: he is on his way now
decisions.reason: The present tense makes the coming sure, as in 24:42-43.

decisions.choice: always
decisions.reason: Readable shows the force of the present command, following the meaning decision.

records.source: Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς δοῦλος καὶ φρόνιμος ὃν κατέστησεν ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκετείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ δοῦναι αὐτοῖς τὴν τροφὴν ἐν καιρῷ;
records.gloss: Who then is the faithful slave and wise whom set the master over the household of him to give to them the food in season?
pieces: Who, then, is the servant that is trustworthy and sensible, whom the master has put in charge of his household staff to give them their food when it is due?

L.45: Who then is the faithful and wise slave whom the master set over his household to give them the food in season?

R.45: Who is the servant who is faithful and wise? Suppose a master puts one of his servants in charge of the other servants in his house. That servant must give them their food at the right time.

decisions.choice: who then is: a question that invites the hearers to see themselves as the slave
decisions.reason: The question is answered in 24:46: the faithful slave is the one the master finds doing his work. The disciples are to be that slave.

decisions.choice: slave, household: a trusted slave put over the other household slaves
decisions.reason: In large households a slave could be put in charge of the others, with the care of food and supplies. The word for slave is the same as in 10:24.

decisions.choice: faithful and wise: trustworthy, and sensible in doing what the time requires
decisions.reason: "Faithful" here means reliable. "Wise" is the word used of the man who built on rock (7:24).

decisions.choice: in season: at the proper time
alternatives: in a certain season of the year
decisions.reason: The phrase means at the right time, when the food is due.

decisions.choice: master, his, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The master is a figure in a parable, so his pronouns take no span, though the picture points to Jesus. The word is the same as "Lord" in 24:42.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: trustworthy and sensible
decisions.reason: Balanced uses everyday words for the two qualities, following the meaning decision.

records.heading: The servant the master finds at work

records.source: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει οὕτως ποιοῦντα·
records.gloss: Blessed the slave that whom having come the master of him will find so doing;
pieces: That servant will be blessed if, when his master comes, he finds him at that very work.

L.46: Blessed [is] that slave whom his master, when he comes, will find so doing.

R.46: That servant will be blessed if his master comes back and finds him doing his job.

decisions.choice: blessed: in the happy state of those God favors
decisions.reason: As in 5:3-11, the word describes someone well off in God's eyes. Here it is the slave the master rewards.

decisions.choice: so doing: giving the household their food as he was told
decisions.reason: "So" points back to the task of 24:45.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you that over all the possessions of him he will set him.
pieces: Truly I tell you, the master will put him in charge of everything he owns.

L.47: Truly I tell you that he will set him over all his possessions.

R.47: I tell you the truth, the master will put that servant in charge of everything he owns.

decisions.choice: set over all his possessions: the reward of faithful work is greater trust
decisions.reason: The faithful slave is given more to care for, as in the parable that follows (25:21, 23).

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The same forms as in 24:2.

decisions.choice: the master; that servant (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is who.

records.source: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ κακὸς δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· Χρονίζει μου ὁ κύριος, καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς συνδούλους αὐτοῦ, ἐσθίῃ δὲ καὶ πίνῃ μετὰ τῶν μεθυόντων, ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει, καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ὑποκριτῶν θήσει· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
records.gloss: If but says the evil slave that in the heart of him, Delays my the master, \v 49 and begins to beat the fellow slaves of him, eats and drinks with those being drunk, \v 50 will come the master of the slave that in day in which not he expects and in hour which not he knows, \v 51 and will cut in two him and the portion of him with the hypocrites will put; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth.
pieces: But that servant may be wicked. He may think to himself, 'My master is a long time coming,'
and start to beat his fellow servants, while he eats and drinks with drunkards.
If so, his master will come on a day he does not look for, at an hour he does not know.
The master will cut him in pieces and put him with the hypocrites, where people will weep and grind their teeth.

L.48: But if that evil slave says in his heart, 'My master is delaying,'
L.49: and begins to beat his fellow slaves, and eats and drinks with the drunkards,
L.50: the master of that slave will come on a day when he does not expect [him] and at an hour that he does not know,
L.51: and will cut him in two and assign him his portion with the hypocrites; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

R.48: But suppose that servant is evil. He says to himself, 'My master will not come back for a long time.'
R.49: So he begins to beat the other servants. He eats and drinks with people who get drunk.
R.50: Then the master will come back on a day when the servant does not expect him, at a time he does not know.
R.51: The master will punish him terribly and put him with the hypocrites. There they will cry and grind their teeth.

decisions.choice: that evil slave: the same slave of 24:45, if he turns out wicked
decisions.reason: "That" points back to the slave put in charge. The same position can be used faithfully or abused.

decisions.choice: cut him in two: the severest punishment
alternatives: cut him off from the household
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut in two, a known form of execution. Yet the slave is then given a place with the hypocrites, so many read it as a picture of severe punishment, or as being cut off from the master's people.

decisions.choice: weeping and gnashing of teeth: exclusion and anguish
decisions.reason: As in 8:12, the words picture the grief and rage of those shut out of the kingdom. Matthew repeats the phrase (13:42, 50; 22:13; 25:30).

decisions.choice: the hypocrites: those whose devotion is a pretense
decisions.reason: As in 6:2 and chapter 23, the word means people who act a part. The slave served his master in name but not in deed.

decisions.choice: where people will weep and grind their teeth (B); There they will cry and grind their teeth (R)
alternatives: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth
decisions.reason: The wording of 8:12 is kept at each level.

decisions.choice: cut him in pieces (B); punish him terribly (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture. Readable gives its meaning, following the meaning decision; if the picture means being cut off, "punish" still holds.

decisions.choice: My master is a long time coming (B); My master will not come back for a long time (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the delay means to the slave: he thinks there is plenty of time.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".
